parsed.rationale: Both `CacheLoader` (package `Caching`) and `MetadataLoader` (package `Metadata`) share three identical members — `cacheKey:String`, `invalidate:() async`, and `lastLoadedAt:Date?` — and differ only in the return type of `load`: `Data` vs `PlaycutMetadata`. This is the canonical PAT pattern: a single protocol with an `associatedtype Payload` and a `load:() async throws -> Payload` requirement would unify both interfaces without loss of type safety. `CacheLoader` would conform with `Payload == Data` and `MetadataLoader` with `Payload == PlaycutMetadata`. Neither record carries any restraint flag (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` are all false), so the refactor is safe to pursue. The shared field count of 4 with only one differing slot strongly supports a generic abstraction rather than two parallel protocols.
